Each X-FAB foundry customer has released numerous SiC chip MOSFETs/JFETs/diodes products — in the 600 V, 700 V, 900 V, 1200 V, and 1700 V ratings. Additionally, each company has utilized their X-FAB-fabricated SiC chips to release numerous modules of various topology, voltage, and current ratings. • Microchip was the first large company to bring 3.3 kV MOSFETs to market, followed by Wolfspeed; Microchip also commercialized 700 kV MOSFETs. • GeneSiC brought 3.3 kV and 6.5 kV MOSFETs to market, as well as MOSFETs of lower voltages. • GE utilized X-FAB for its 1200V and 1.7 kV MOSFETs. GE then commercialized 1200 V and 1.7 kV SiC, as well as 600 V high-power GaN modules, and did significant work on 3.3 kV and 6.5 kV modules, which are now available as engineering samples. • Monolith (acquired by Littelfuse) brought 1200 V and 1.7 kV diodes and MOSFETs to market. • Wolfspeed commercialized 1.7 kV modules and did significant work on 3.3 kV, 6.5 kV, and 10 kV modules, which are available as engineering samples. • Navitas and Transphorm developed GaN modules and application circuits for insertion of their 650 V chips; dozens of products from different cellphone and laptop power supply manufactures now use Navitas and Transphorm GaN chips. • Infineon (which acquired GaN Systems) is commercializing bidirectional GaN chips that have applications in energy storage, electric vehicle charging, and other areas. With respect to other power electronics products: • Atom Power has a line of SiC-based circuit breaker products used in residential and EV fast-charging applications. • John Deere offers hybrid loaders. • ABB offers SiC-based U.S.-manufactured UPS products and GaN-based 48V-1V Single-stage LLC Converters. • Lockheed Martin’s collaborative projects have produced high-frequency GaN power converters for its systems. • Toshiba has developed SiC-based hybrid PV Inverters with Li-ion Battery Integration and also commercialized SiC chip-based High-Speed Medium-Voltage Motor Drives. United Technologies manufactures SiC- and Gan-based active harmonic filters for Variable Frequency Drive and Grid Tied Inverter Applications. CREATING A VIBRANT & ENGAGED WBG ECOSYSTEM PowerAmerica has had a positive, measurable impact on power semiconductor development and manufacturing in the U.S. From 2015 to present, the technology has matured considerably; commercial applications have grown; sales volumes of SiC and GaN have multiplied; and companies across the supply chain have grown and prospered. We have brought together many of the country’s leading companies and academic researchers, as well as national labs and other stakeholders, to forge new partnerships that address key challenges. PowerAmerica members regularly report that one of the primary benefits they derive from membership is the networking and information exchange that takes place at our semi-annual events.
